newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Bulk of Indonesia's Busang gold seen recoverable.
newsitem.headline: Bulk of Indonesia's Busang gold seen recoverable.

text.p: Much of the gold in the huge Busang property in Indonesia's East Kalimantan province would be recoverable, but production costs would depend on the skill of the mine operator, industry sources said on Friday.
Canadian exploration company Bre-X Minerals Ltd which discovered the motherlode, said last Monday Busang was estimated to contain some 71 million ounces of gold.
But its vice-president of exploration, John Felderhof, said on Wednesday the next estimate expected in mid-April would put the resource at about 95 million ounces.
"If you would ask me what is the total potential, I would feel very comfortable with 200 million ounces," he said.
"With the advances in technology, 75 to 80 percent of the gold should be recoverable," an Indonesian geologist whose company is involved in gold mining told Reuters.
"Busang will involve primary mining, and drilling is expected to be go well beyond 400 metres where the preliminary results were obtained," he said, declining to be identified.
Industry sources said the cost of ensuring the environment was not badly damaged by the mining were expected to be lower than, for instance, in the United States, but would be fairly large.
The Indonesian government on Tuesday approved a deal by Bre-X to develop the property jointly with its Indonesian partners and Freeport McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc of the United States.
Bre-X will take a 45-percent stake in Busang, Freeport 15 percent, and PT Askatindo Karya Mineral and PT Amsya Lyna a combined 30 percent. The rest goes to the Indonesian government.

Askatindo and Amsya are each 50-percent owned by the Nusamba group, which is 80 percent owned by three foundations headed by President Suharto, and 10 percent each by his eldest son Sigit Harjojudanto and business tycoon Muhammad "Bob" Hasan.
An Indonesian mining analyst said she would expect proven reserves in the Busang property to be around 70 million ounces, with the rest being probable and less than probable reserves.

"This is what you could call is my guesstimate," she said, adding that there was little doubt the Busang property contained a huge amount of gold but a lack of anything more than data from preliminary drilling made detailed analysis difficult.
"I expect the operator to do hard rock mining, digging deep to get at the gold," she said.
The Indonesian geologist said a skilled operator could keep costs at around $160 an ounce.
"In this case, Freeport is an experienced miner and costs are expected to be kept to a minimum," he said.

Bre-X itself on Wednesday estimated capital costs for the mine at around $1.5 billion with cash costs "significantly less" than the $96 per ounce it had earlier estimated. It said production was expected to begin in 2000 at a rate of two million ounces annually, rising to four million in 2002.
Freeport operates one of the world's largest copper and gold mines in Indonesia's Irian Jaya province through its 80.28-percent unit Freeport Indonesia.

The geologist also said Busang's owners would have to allocate a large amount of money as environmental costs, adding that in the United States as much as $50 per ounce of gold was set aside for such requirements.
"Although not as much would be required in Indonesia, environmental concern here is catching up...and so will the costs," he said.
